content.user_title: Build Azure Event Grid Workflows in .NET
content.value_statement: Azure Event Grid applications require careful choices across schemas, authentication, publishing, and delivery handling. This skill provides focused .NET SDK patterns for those decisions.
actual_capabilities: Explains package selection for Event Grid topics, domains, namespaces, and CloudEvents integration.
Compares API key, SAS token, and Microsoft Entra ID authentication patterns.
Guides single, batch, domain-routed, EventGridEvent, and CloudEvent publishing.
Describes namespace pull delivery with receive, acknowledge, release, and reject operations.
Shows Azure Functions triggers and parsing for EventGridEvent, CloudEvent, and system event data.
Provides error handling and regional failover patterns for Event Grid clients.
limitations: The skill provides guidance and examples but does not create Azure resources or execute deployments.
Users must supply valid endpoints, identities, credentials, topic names, and Azure permissions.
Examples use placeholders and simplified application types that require adaptation and testing.
Package versions and service limits can change, so users should verify current Microsoft documentation.

use_cases.title: Publish application events
use_cases.description: Create a .NET publisher for single or batched EventGridEvent and CloudEvent messages.

use_cases.title: Design secure event integration
use_cases.description: Compare schemas, authentication methods, domain routing, and regional failover before implementation.

use_cases.title: Process delivered events
use_cases.description: Build Azure Functions triggers or namespace receivers with correct acknowledgement and retry behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Choose packages and authentication
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend the Event Grid .NET packages and authentication method for [delivery model], [hosting environment], and [identity constraints].
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new Event Grid project

prompt_templates.title: Create a publisher
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a .NET publisher for [event schema], [event type], and [batching needs] using [authentication method].

prompt_templates.title: Design pull delivery processing
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a namespace receiver for [event volume] with acknowledgement, release, rejection, idempotency, and partial failure handling.

prompt_templates.title: Plan resilient event architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my [architecture summary] and propose schema validation, managed identity, batching, dead-lettering, retry, and regional failover decisions.

output_examples.input: Choose authentication for an Azure-hosted publisher without stored secrets.
output: Use Microsoft Entra ID through DefaultAzureCredential.
Assign the publisher identity only the required Event Grid data sender role.
Keep the endpoint in configuration and test authorization before production.

output_examples.input: Plan pull delivery handling for events that may fail independently.
output: Receive a bounded batch and process each event independently.
Acknowledge successful lock tokens and release retryable failures.
Reject invalid events and configure dead-letter handling.
Make handlers idempotent because delivery can repeat.

output_examples.input: Compare EventGridEvent and CloudEvent for a portable integration.
output_examples.output: CloudEvent is the preferred choice for cross-platform interoperability. EventGridEvent fits Azure-specific integrations that depend on its native schema.

best_practices: Prefer managed identity and least-privilege roles instead of long-lived access keys.
Use idempotent handlers, schema validation, and explicit acknowledgement decisions.
Batch compatible events and test service limits, retries, dead-lettering, and failover.
anti_patterns: Do not embed access keys, SAS tokens, or production endpoints in source code.
Do not acknowledge events before processing completes successfully.
Do not treat every failure as retryable or ignore repeated delivery.

faq.question: Which .NET package supports Event Grid topics and domains?
faq.answer: Use Azure.Messaging.EventGrid for push delivery through topics and domains.

faq.question: Which package supports namespace pull delivery?
faq.answer: Use Azure.Messaging.EventGrid.Namespaces for sending to namespace topics and receiving from subscriptions.

faq.question: Should I use EventGridEvent or CloudEvent?
faq.answer: Use CloudEvent for portability. Use EventGridEvent when an Azure-specific schema is appropriate.

faq.question: What authentication method is preferred?
faq.answer: Prefer Microsoft Entra ID with managed identity. Use access keys or SAS tokens only when required.

faq.question: How should failed pull-delivery events be handled?
faq.answer: Release retryable failures, reject invalid events, and acknowledge only successful processing.

faq.question: Does this skill deploy Azure Event Grid resources?
faq.answer: No. It provides .NET SDK guidance and examples but does not provision resources or run deployments.
